info.title: RF backend API
info.description: HTTP surface for the Rust RF backend. Frontend calls go via Next.js route handlers at `/api/v2/*`, which bridge the Supabase session cookie to a bearer JWT before forwarding here.

CreateMaterialTypeBody.description:
Request body for POST — mandatory `name`, everything else
optional. The handler validates constraints through the use
case; the adapter maps a DB unique violation to a stable
`DUPLICATE_NAME` conflict code.

CreatePurchaseOrderBody.description: Body for POST. `status` defaults to `draft` server-side if omitted.

CreateRollBody.description:
Create body. Caller sends `material_type_id`; the server looks
up the corresponding name. Any `material_type` string in the
body is ignored.

CutHistoryDto.description:
Response DTO — thin wrapper over the domain entry. Separated from
`CutHistoryEntry` so the HTTP contract can evolve independently
of domain schema. Today the mapping is 1:1; renaming / derived
fields will land here first when we start splitting concerns.

percentage.description: Percentage growth vs. the prior 7 days.

oneOf.description:
The embedded material_types row, present on list/get, absent
on create/update response (PostgREST Prefer:
return=representation doesn't include embeds).

MaterialTypeDto.description:
Response DTO — mirrors the domain struct 1:1 today. Separated
from `MaterialType` so the HTTP contract can evolve without
reaching into the domain type.

PurchaseOrderDto.description:
Response DTO — mirrors the domain struct. Separate so the HTTP
surface can diverge from the domain without a domain change.

UpdateMaterialTypeBody.description:
Request body for PUT. Every field is optional so the HTTP surface
can evolve to PATCH semantics later without breaking callers —
for now, the UI always sends a full replacement. Nullable fields
use `Option<Option<T>>` via `serde_with`-style manual handling:
`null` in JSON explicitly clears the column, omitted means leave
as-is.

To keep the DTO simple we expose the fields as plain `Option<T>`
here. Semantics: present-and-non-null replaces the column,
present-and-null is the same as omitting (the UI today never
needs to explicitly null a column). If that distinction matters
later we'll promote to `Option<Option<T>>` + a custom visitor.

UpdatePurchaseOrderBody.description:
Body for PUT — status is NOT on this type. Status changes go
through `PUT /api/v2/po/{id}/status` (Task 3), which enforces the
state machine + blocks `received` from the generic path.

UpdateSupplierBody.description:
Update body — all fields optional. Single-level `Option<T>` for
simplicity; explicit null-ing of columns isn't something the UI
needs today. When it does, promote to Option<Option<T>>.

supabase_jwt.description: Supabase-issued RS256 JWT. Forwarded to PostgREST so RLS scopes rows to the caller.
